checks.expected_narration: Now select Localized defect near x one equals zero point three five. Keep the amplitude at zero point two five and begin with forty one points. The area percentage is approximately two point zero one three, and the differential score is approximately one point six seven two. Both are below five. However, the local residual graph contains a distinct negative trough near zero point three five. A criterion based on an average can dilute an error that occupies only a narrow region. That is why you must inspect the plotted residual as well as the scorecard. Record the forty one point results before changing Sampling resolution to one hundred sixty one points. The area percentage becomes approximately one point nine four two, while the differential score becomes approximately one point five six six. The trough remains, and the denser grid describes its shape with more points. Neither result changes to an automatic failure. A screenshot with the trough marked near zero point three five is useful evidence for E one. Avoid claiming that this finite-difference exercise validates a laboratory dataset or duplicates the NIST point-test implementation.

checks.title: Modeling and saved evidence · 65–95 min
checks.focus: Export, shared workspace, restore inputs, then refit; stored results are not a fresh calculation.
checks.expected_narration: For D five, return Controlled perturbation to Consistent reference and Sampling resolution to forty one points. Verify those settings before pressing Run modeling test. The application reports convergence using thirty nine interior points, with no fitted parameter at a bound. The two pure endpoints are excluded from this fitting step. Pressure and vapor-composition errors both round to zero point zero zero zero on the scorecard. They are very small numerical errors, not a promise of exact experimental accuracy. This synthetic reference is generated from the same family of consistent activity models, so a very close reproduction is expected. Under Inspect, choose Modeling residuals to see both pressure and vapor-composition residuals. The method fits two constant NRTL interaction parameters for this isothermal case, with the nonrandomness parameter fixed at zero point four seven. It asks whether the selected model reproduces the observations under the stated vapor-property approximation. It does not independently prove that observations obey every thermodynamic constraint. Click Export all results to download the current results and settings. Save the file beside your worksheet, and retain screenshots of the perturbed cases before returning to the clean case. Each export describes the current state; it is not a history of every case you explored. To reopen a case, expand Study workspace, reopen and compare cases, above the calculator. A freshly exported study is already listed in this workspace. For a downloaded file, use Load studies or a comparison JSON. Here I change the current controls, then select Restore Case One from the recorded case. The inputs return to the clean reference at forty one points. The modeling result must be fitted again, so I press Run modeling test and confirm convergence. Restoring inputs does not turn old saved results into a fresh calculation. Do not confuse saving evidence with uploading an assignment.
